paragraphs.context: At this school, you will be learning side by side with dragons
paragraphs.mainIdea: A school for all the tribes.
paragraphs.simple: This page is a welcome letter from Jade Mountain Academy. Young dragons from all the tribes study there together, so the next pages give some facts about each tribe.

paragraphs.context: You have been assigned to a winglet with six other dragons;
paragraphs.mainIdea: Each student is in a winglet.
paragraphs.simple: Every student is put in a small class called a winglet, with six dragons from other tribes. The list of winglets comes on the next page.

background.note: At Jade Mountain Academy, a small class of seven dragonets, one from each tribe.

paragraphs.context: WE WISH YOU ALL THE POWER OF WINGS OF FIRE!
paragraphs.simple: The letter says the students are the hope for a long peace in Pyrrhia. It ends with a wish. "Wings of fire" is a phrase from the old Dragonet Prophecy; here it means "may you be strong and do great things".

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can survive a long time without water, poison enemies with the tips
paragraphs.simple: SandWings can live a long time without water. They can poison enemies with the end of their tail, like a scorpion, hide under the sand, and breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: since the end of the War of SandWing Succession, Queen Thorn
paragraphs.mainIdea: The SandWings have a new queen.
paragraphs.simple: There was a long war about who would be the SandWing queen. That war is over now, and Thorn is the queen.

background.note: The war that began when Queen Oasis died and her three daughters fought to be queen of the SandWings. Most of the tribes joined in.
Thorn is now queen of the SandWings.

paragraphs.context: Students at Jade Mountain: Arid, Onyx, Ostrich, Pronghorn, Qibli
paragraphs.simple: These are the five SandWing students at the school. Each tribe page ends with a list like this.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire (if warm enough), hold their breath for up
paragraphs.simple: MudWings can breathe fire when they are warm, stay under water or mud for an hour without breathing, and hide in mud. They are very strong.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: powerful fighters and fliers, can breathe fire
paragraphs.simple: SkyWings are strong fighters and fast fliers, and they can breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Queen Ruby (although some dragons still support Queen Scarlet,
paragraphs.simple: Ruby is the SkyWing queen now. But some SkyWings still want Scarlet, the old queen who lost her throne. Scarlet may still be alive and hiding somewhere.

background.note: Ruby is Queen Scarlet's daughter. After Scarlet loses her throne, Ruby becomes queen of the SkyWings.
Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.

paragraphs.context: Description: blue or green or aquamarine scales; webs between their claws; gills
paragraphs.simple: SeaWings are blue or green. They have skin between their claws, gills for breathing under water, and stripes that glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can withstand subzero temperatures and bright light, exhale a deadly frostbreath
paragraphs.simple: IceWings can live in very cold places and in bright light, and they breathe out frostbreath, a deadly freezing breath.

background.note: The deadly freezing breath of IceWings; it can freeze and kill other dragons.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can camouflage their scales to blend into their surroundings;
paragraphs.simple: RainWings can change the colors of their scales to hide and match the things around them. They can also shoot deadly venom (poison) from their fangs.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire, disappear into dark shadows; once known for reading minds
paragraphs.simple: NightWings can breathe fire and hide in dark shadows. Long ago they were famous for reading minds and seeing the future, but the guide says they cannot do this anymore.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Queen Glory (see recent scrolls on the NightWing Exodus and
paragraphs.simple: Glory, the RainWing queen, is now the queen of the NightWings too. The page says you can read about how this happened in new scrolls: the NightWings left their old home (the Exodus), and there was a contest for the RainWing throne.

background.note: Glory is a RainWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is the queen of the RainWings, and now of the NightWings too.
The time when the NightWings left their island home.
The contest for the RainWing throne.

paragraphs.context: Beware the darkness of dragons,
paragraphs.simple: This is the Jade Mountain Prophecy, a new message about the future. It starts with warnings. "Beware" means "be careful of". "The darkness of dragons" means dragons who are evil or dangerous. "The stalker of dreams" is someone who follows dragons secretly, even in their dreams.

paragraphs.context: Beware the talons of power and fire,
paragraphs.simple: "Talons" are a dragon's claws. "The talons of power and fire" means a strong, dangerous dragon. The next line warns about a female dragon who is not what she seems: she hides who she really is.

paragraphs.context: Something is coming to shake the earth,
paragraphs.simple: Something terrible is coming. It will shake the ground and burn it. The prophecy does not say what it is.

paragraphs.context: Jade Mountain will fall beneath thunder and ice
paragraphs.simple: Here "fall" means "be destroyed". Jade Mountain, where the school is, will be destroyed by thunder and ice, unless dragons can find "the lost city of night". The prophecy does not say what the thunder and ice are, or where that city is.

background.note: A tall mountain in the middle of Pyrrhia with many caves inside it.

paragraphs.context: The volcano was restless, and so were the dragons in
paragraphs.mainIdea: A restless night on the volcano.
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings live in a stone fortress on a volcano. Tonight the volcano is shaking, and many dragons are awake and nervous.

background.note: Purple-black dragons with silver scales under their wings, like a night sky full of stars. Many dragons believe they can read minds and see the future.

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper felt the mountain rumble under her talons as she
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper rushes through the stone halls in the middle of the night. She does not want anyone to see where she is going, but other dragons look at her with curiosity.

background.note: Secretkeeper is Moon's mother.

paragraphs.context: She didn’t need to count days to know. Her bones
paragraphs.mainIdea: She knows tonight is the night.
paragraphs.simple: She does not need to count the days. Her whole body tells her that tonight her egg will hatch, and she must hurry without being caught.

paragraphs.context: She imagined hungry panthers prowling the undergrowth, dangerous crocodiles with
paragraphs.simple: She imagines all the things that could hurt a lonely egg in the forest: wild cats, crocodiles, or careless dragons.

paragraphs.context: Just before she reached the ledge, she passed Mastermind and
paragraphs.mainIdea: Two dragons she does not want to meet.
paragraphs.simple: On her way out she passes two important NightWings. Mastermind looks at her hard, and she is afraid he knows her secret.

background.note: Mastermind is a NightWing scientist who does experiments. He is Starflight's father.
Farsight is Starflight's mother.

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper winced; her name had never sounded more appropriate. Sometimes
paragraphs.mainIdea: Her name fits her too well.
paragraphs.simple: "Secretkeeper" means "a dragon who keeps secrets." She wonders if her name made her become a dragon with a huge secret.

paragraphs.context: “Do you want company?” Farsight asked. Behind her, Mastermind frowned
paragraphs.simple: Farsight offers to stay with her. Farsight also lost an egg once: Morrowseer took it away from her.

background.note: Morrowseer is a big, scary NightWing. Years ago he told the Talons of Peace about the Dragonet Prophecy.

paragraphs.context: “It’s not the same at all!” she snapped, shooting a
paragraphs.simple: To make Farsight go away, Secretkeeper says something hurtful. She reminds Farsight that her son is far away on the continent, spoiled and admired by the Talons of Peace.

background.note: A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: She took a running leap off the ledge and soared
paragraphs.simple: She jumps off the ledge and flies over the black beach. The volcano rumbles, the clouds glow red, and the air smells terrible. She heads for the cave.

paragraphs.context: Only one guard tonight. Nobody really believed any of the
paragraphs.simple: A secret tunnel joins the NightWings' island to the rainforest. Usually the guard is asleep, so she can sneak past.

background.note: The thick, hot, wet forest in Pyrrhia where the RainWings live. The books call the RainWings' home 'the rainforest'.

paragraphs.context: But not tonight. Preyhunter was sitting out on the ledge
paragraphs.simple: Tonight a guard called Preyhunter is awake, watching the volcano nervously.

background.note: Preyhunter is a NightWing.

paragraphs.context: “Do you think it’ll be tonight?” he asked her as
paragraphs.mainIdea: He does not know her secret.
paragraphs.simple: At first she is afraid Preyhunter has guessed her secret, but he is only worried about the volcano. Many NightWings have lost eggs, so he does not remember hers.

paragraphs.context: “I’ll be all right,” Secretkeeper said. “I just — can’t
paragraphs.simple: She says she cannot sleep and wants to hunt a gift for Greatness to give to the queen.

background.note: Princess Greatness is a NightWing princess.

paragraphs.context: She fell through into the clearest, most brightly lit night
paragraphs.mainIdea: A very bright night in the rainforest.
paragraphs.simple: She comes out in the rainforest. The night is very bright, because two of the three moons are full, so a RainWing might see her.

background.note: Dragons of the rainforest whose scales change colour. They can hide by matching the colours around them, and they can shoot venom from their fangs.
The dragon world has three moons. Dragons say 'Three moons!' when they are surprised or upset, the way people say 'Oh my goodness!'

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper scrabbled frantically in the dark hollow. It couldn’t be
paragraphs.simple: Her egg is not in its hiding place. She searches wildly and blames herself for leaving it there.

paragraphs.context: I only wanted to protect her from that island
paragraphs.simple: She hid the egg because she did not want her dragonet to grow up on the island, with its smoke, rules and fear of the volcano.

paragraphs.context: At least, it had to be her egg — but
paragraphs.simple: She finds the egg in the moonlight, but it is no longer black. Now it is a strange silver color, like a piece of the full moon.

paragraphs.context: She’d never seen a hatching before. There were so few
paragraphs.mainIdea: She has never seen a hatching.
paragraphs.simple: Very few eggs hatch on the island, and only a few dragons may watch, because the NightWings are afraid of making the new dragonets sick.

background.note: The NightWings' secret home: an island with a volcano. A magic tunnel joins it to the rainforest.

paragraphs.context: If she hadn’t lied to everyone — about having stomach
paragraphs.simple: She told everyone that her egg broke and that she buried the pieces. If she had kept the egg on the island, she could have watched the hatching of Mightyclaws and learned how it works.

background.note: Mightyclaws is a young NightWing who is friendly to Starflight.

paragraphs.context: So Secretkeeper had no idea what to do. She’d never
paragraphs.simple: She does not know what to do. She is afraid she did something wrong that hurt the dragonet inside.

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper stared at her in awe. She was perfect, perfect
paragraphs.simple: The dragonet is perfect and looks healthier than any NightWing she knows. This is the reason she took such a big risk.

paragraphs.context: She wished she could share this moment with the dragonet’s
paragraphs.simple: She wishes the father could see this moment, but she cannot trust him. He would tell the tribe and the dragonet would have to grow up on the island.

paragraphs.context: “I’m your mother, little one,” she whispered. “I’m going to
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper names her daughter Moonwatcher, because the dragonet keeps looking at the moons. She promises her a long, happy life.

background.note: Moonwatcher, usually called Moon, is a young NightWing. She can hear other dragons' thoughts and sometimes sees the future.

paragraphs.context: Then she came fully awake and realized what would happen
paragraphs.simple: If Preyhunter finds them, Moonwatcher will be taken to the island and Secretkeeper will be punished.

paragraphs.context: “No, I can’t stay,” Secretkeeper said. “I’m sorry. You’ll be
paragraphs.simple: She has to leave the dragonet alone. Hiding an egg was easy, but hiding a dragonet who moves and squeaks is much harder.

paragraphs.context: Is it possible? The scrolls say NightWings once had mind
paragraphs.simple: Old scrolls say NightWings could once read minds. Secretkeeper always thought it was just a story to make other tribes afraid, but Moonwatcher seems to read her thoughts.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking. Some NightWings, like Moon, have it; a dragon who can do this is a 'mind reader'.
A long roll of paper with writing on it. Dragons keep their books, maps and letters as scrolls.

paragraphs.context: “See you soon, little one,” Secretkeeper whispered. Her claws wanted
paragraphs.simple: Leaving is the hardest thing she has ever done. She hopes her tears will stop Preyhunter from asking questions.

paragraphs.context: She was alone, with the shadows firmly wrapped around her
paragraphs.simple: Moonwatcher is alone, with only her mother's scary thoughts in her mind. She has learned that the world is frightening without her mother.

paragraphs.context: “I don’t want you to leave me here,” Moon said.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Moon does not want her mother to leave.
paragraphs.simple: Moon sits under her mother's wing and feels that this is where she belongs. She does not want to be left alone at the new school.

paragraphs.context: They’d found a spot under a tree where they could
paragraphs.simple: They watch new students arrive. There are so many big, noisy dragons that Moon feels small and afraid of being stepped on.

background.note: Big, strong brown dragons who live in the swamps of the Mud Kingdom. They can hold their breath for up to an hour and hide in mud.

paragraphs.context: And what if they hated her? She wouldn’t even have
paragraphs.simple: Moon thinks other dragons will hate her just for being a NightWing, and other NightWings already dislike her for being different.

paragraphs.context: “I know,” her mother said kindly. “But you have to.
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper says the school will be good for Moon. In her mind she adds that at least there will not be many NightWings there. Moon can hear this thought.

background.note: A tall mountain in the middle of Pyrrhia with many caves inside it.

paragraphs.context: “Most of them are awful and you know it,” Secretkeeper
paragraphs.simple: When Secretkeeper brought Moon to the tribe six months ago, the other NightWings were jealous and unfriendly. The volcano destroyed their island, so the NightWings now live in the rainforest. Queen Glory forgave Secretkeeper, but others did not.

background.note: Glory is a RainWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She can change the colour of her scales and shoot venom.
Sunny is a small SandWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is cheerful and always hopes for the best.
Starflight is a NightWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is shy and very clever, and he loves reading scrolls.

paragraphs.context: “I want to be with you,” Moon replied simply. It
paragraphs.simple: Moon finally has her mother every day, after years of only short secret visits, and now she has to leave her again.

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper crouched and put her face right in front of
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper reminds Moon not to answer thoughts she hears. Everyone believes NightWings have no powers now, so Moon must hide her mind reading, which her mother calls a "curse."

paragraphs.context: “I know,” Moon answered. “Stay secret. Stay hidden. Stay safe.”
paragraphs.simple: For years the NightWings pretended they could read minds. Now they are truly afraid of any dragon who really can.

paragraphs.context: Moon frowned up at her mother. She was glad the
paragraphs.mainIdea: Moon wishes she could answer back.
paragraphs.simple: Moon hears her mother think that she is too nervous. Moon wishes she could reply that maybe there is a good reason for it.

paragraphs.context: “Oh, look,” Secretkeeper said obliviously, her eyes lighting up. She
paragraphs.simple: Blue and green dragons fly down. Secretkeeper thinks the one wearing many pearls is their queen.

background.note: Blue or green dragons who live in the sea. They can breathe underwater, and the stripes on their scales glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: “Queen Coral,” Moon recited. One thing she could do
paragraphs.simple: Moon recognizes Queen Coral of the SeaWings. Studying is something Moon is good at, so she has learned a lot before coming to school.

background.note: Queen Coral is the queen of the SeaWings and Tsunami's mother.
The school inside Jade Mountain where young dragons from all seven tribes learn together. The dragonets of destiny started it.

paragraphs.context: Moon stared down at her claws. It was pretty clear
paragraphs.simple: Moon can tell that her mother cares more about other dragons liking Moon than about Moon liking them.

paragraphs.context: Oh, I’m a snail-brain, she realized. That must be Tsunami.
paragraphs.simple: Moon calls herself stupid ("snail-brain") for not seeing it sooner: the blue SeaWing is Tsunami, the princess from the famous prophecy.

background.note: Tsunami is a SeaWing princess, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is brave and likes to be the leader.
A message that tells what will happen in the future. NightWings who can see the future give prophecies.

paragraphs.context: “It’ll be great,” Tsunami promised the queen. “I’ll take care
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami will look after her sister.
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami promises to take care of her sister Anemone at the school.

background.note: Anemone is a young SeaWing princess, Tsunami's sister. She is an animus: she can put magic into things.

paragraphs.context: “Maybe next year, Auklet,” Tsunami said. The little dragon beamed
paragraphs.simple: The tiny dragonet is Auklet, another of Tsunami's sisters. She is too young for school.

background.note: Auklet is Tsunami's little sister, a SeaWing princess.

paragraphs.context: Was it because her mother thought she was cursed? Maybe
paragraphs.mainIdea: Does her mother want her far away?
paragraphs.simple: Moon wonders if her mother sends her away because she thinks Moon is cursed. Over the years Moon has learned to block some of her mother's thoughts.

paragraphs.context: “Who’s this?” Tsunami asked, turning to the last SeaWing dragonet
paragraphs.simple: A dark green SeaWing sits behind the queen. He is a little plump and calm. He wears no jewels, only a gold armband with shiny black stones.

paragraphs.context: “Turtle,” he said, shooting Tsunami a friendly smile.
paragraphs.simple: His name is Turtle. He is one of Tsunami's brothers.

background.note: Turtle is a quiet SeaWing prince and a student at Jade Mountain Academy. He is Tsunami's brother.

paragraphs.context: “One of my brothers?” Tsunami echoed. “I didn’t realize
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami is surprised. A magic statue made by Orca killed the queen's female eggs, but the male eggs survived, so Tsunami has many brothers.

background.note: Orca was a SeaWing princess and animus. A statue she put magic into later harmed the eggs of Queen Coral's daughters.

paragraphs.context: “Who cares about them?” Coral asked. “They can’t inherit the
paragraphs.mainIdea: The queen does not care about her sons.
paragraphs.simple: Coral says the sons do not matter, because only daughters can become queen.

paragraphs.context: That was strange. Moon had only met a few dragons
paragraphs.simple: Only a few dragons can hide their thoughts from Moon. Queen Glory does it without trying when she feels uncomfortable, the same way she stops her scales from showing her feelings.

paragraphs.context: Turtle wasn’t like Glory or those NightWings, though; his mind
paragraphs.simple: Turtle's mind does not feel like a wall hiding secrets. It is just calm and quiet, and Moon wonders how he does it.

paragraphs.context: As the SeaWings disappeared into the cave, Turtle looked back
paragraphs.simple: When Turtle looks back, Moon feels dizzy and sees a picture of the future in pieces, like a puzzle.

paragraphs.context: And Turtle pinning Anemone to the sand as the white-pink
paragraphs.simple: In the vision, Turtle holds Anemone down on a beach while she twists in pain.

paragraphs.context: But she knew. She’d known since she read the scrolls
paragraphs.mainIdea: Moon knows what the vision was.
paragraphs.simple: Old scrolls say NightWings can read minds and see the future. Moon now understands that her nightmares are really visions of the future.

paragraphs.context: What she didn’t know was whether the visions were inevitable
paragraphs.simple: She does not know if her visions must come true, what they mean, or what to do about them. She seems to be the first NightWing in hundreds of years with these powers.

background.note: The large land (continent) where all the dragon tribes in these books live.

paragraphs.context: And if the other NightWings wouldn’t be able to handle
paragraphs.simple: If dragons fear mind reading, they will fear visions too. Moon has not even told her mother. One "curse" is bad enough.

paragraphs.context: Turtle hadn’t looked sinister at all, despite the weird blankness
paragraphs.simple: Turtle did not look evil. Moon wonders if he will change when he is older, or if he is just very good at hiding who he really is.

paragraphs.context: “Queen Glory is barely older than you are,” Secretkeeper answered.
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper means that Queen Coral has ruled for many years, while Glory is still very young.

paragraphs.context: Moon studied her mother sideways. Many of the NightWings harbored
paragraphs.simple: Many NightWings are angry that a RainWing is now their queen, but Moon does not think her mother is one of them.

paragraphs.context: Secretkeeper took a step back, averting her face, and Moon
paragraphs.simple: Moon hears a thought her mother tried to bury: Secretkeeper is not sure that leaving Moon here is the right thing.

paragraphs.context: “Trust me, moonbud,” her mother said, cupping Moon’s snout in
paragraphs.simple: Secretkeeper calls Moon "moonbud," a loving name. She tells her to hide her "curse," act normal and write soon.

paragraphs.context: Moon stayed under the tree for a while, decidedly not
paragraphs.simple: There are only thirty-five students, and it is an honor to be invited. Moon does not understand why she was chosen.

paragraphs.context: Well, then, she thought, when she couldn’t put it off
paragraphs.simple: Moon remembers being alone and hungry in the rainforest as a little dragonet. If she was brave enough then, she can be brave enough to walk into the school.

paragraphs.context: “Hello!” a voice accosted her loudly, while Moon’s eyes were
paragraphs.simple: A NightWing greets Moon at the entrance and jokes that she can read minds. Moon is frightened that her secret is already known.

paragraphs.context: “Just kidding,” said the older NightWing. “MAAAAYBE. I’m Fatespeaker. I’m
paragraphs.simple: The NightWing is Fatespeaker, who is helping at the school. She gives Moon a welcome scroll and a map.

background.note: Fatespeaker is a cheerful young NightWing. She believes she can see the future.

paragraphs.context: “Yes. Um. Moon.” Now she recognized this NightWing, which she
paragraphs.simple: Moon knows only two NightWings, besides her mother, whose minds are not dark and worried: thoughtful Starflight and hopeful Fatespeaker. Both chose to live with the RainWings.

paragraphs.context: She glanced around, wondering hopefully if Starflight was nearby. He
paragraphs.simple: Starflight was the NightWing in the false prophecy. He lost his sight when the volcano exploded, and Fatespeaker usually guides him.

paragraphs.context: The enormous entrance cave looked as though it could fit
paragraphs.simple: The entrance cave is huge, bright and full of stalactites, some so long that they reach the floor.

paragraphs.context: “Moon, Moon, Moon,” Fatespeaker muttered, rolling a scroll between her
paragraphs.simple: Fatespeaker tells Moon where her cave is and says she will love her clawmates.

background.note: At Jade Mountain Academy, a dragon who shares your sleeping cave.

paragraphs.context: “Oooo, here come some IceWings!” Fatespeaker cried. “Want to stick
paragraphs.simple: Fatespeaker is excited to see IceWings arriving. Moon is too nervous to meet them, and the two ice dragons look proud and unfriendly.

background.note: Silver-white or pale blue dragons from the frozen north of Pyrrhia. They can live in great cold and breathe out a deadly freezing breath (frostbreath).

paragraphs.context: “Fifth cave on the right,” Moon murmured to herself, moving
paragraphs.simple: Colored glass lamps hang along the tunnel. It feels more like the sunny rainforest than an underground cave.

paragraphs.context: Soon the tunnel straightened out, and Moon could see small
paragraphs.simple: Many students are already in their caves. Moon can hear all their thoughts at once, and they crowd into her head.

paragraphs.context: Moon scrunched her eyes shut, trying to hold back the
paragraphs.simple: The noise reminds her of joining the NightWing village, where everyone's thoughts were angry and unfriendly. She was used to the quiet rainforest.

paragraphs.context: They still echoed in there, even though the NightWings were
paragraphs.simple: Moon still remembers what the NightWings thought about her: that it was unfair, that she did not know their suffering on the volcano, and that she could never be one of them.

paragraphs.context: Mostly she’d dealt with the NightWing noise by escaping to
paragraphs.simple: In the village she escaped the noise by flying to a tall tree or a waterfall. Here she will be stuck with other dragons all the time.

paragraphs.context: Moon opened her eyes again and fixed her gaze on
paragraphs.simple: Moon passes two SandWings, and one of them watches her closely.

background.note: The desert dragons of Pyrrhia. They have pale gold scales and a poisonous barb on the end of the tail, and they can live a long time without water.

paragraphs.context: NightWing flashed through his head. Thorn doesn’t like them; we
paragraphs.simple: He thinks about Queen Thorn, NightWing prisoners and whether NightWings really have no powers. He notices Moon looks nervous and wonders if she is shy or up to something.

background.note: Thorn is a strong SandWing.

paragraphs.context: It was nicer than she’d expected. The doorway made up
paragraphs.simple: The cave has three beds: a rock ledge, a pile of leaves and moss, and a hammock. They seem made for three different kinds of dragon.

paragraphs.context: Moon slid her welcome scroll and her map scroll into
paragraphs.simple: There are scrolls for everyone to read, about history, adventures, legends and animals. These are exactly the kinds of things Moon likes.

paragraphs.context: She noticed that there weren’t any of the recent scrolls
paragraphs.simple: There are no scrolls about the dragonets of the prophecy and how they ended the war. Moon guesses the dragonets find those stories embarrassing.

background.note: The war that began when Queen Oasis died and her three daughters fought to be queen of the SandWings. Most of the tribes joined in.
The five dragonets of the prophecy: Clay, Tsunami, Glory, Starflight and Sunny. 'Destiny' means what is sure to happen in the future.

paragraphs.context: Is this for one of my clawmates? Am I going
paragraphs.simple: Moon finds a scroll for learning the alphabet and wonders if one of her clawmates is very young.

paragraphs.context: Out of nowhere, Moon felt a sudden burst of angry
paragraphs.simple: Suddenly Moon feels a burst of angry thoughts like a spear in her head. Two dragons are shouting in the hall.

paragraphs.context: “Don’t you dare blow smoke in my face —” She
paragraphs.simple: The dragons fighting outside remember the war: the SeaWing thinks the SkyWing might have helped destroy the SeaWings' Summer Palace.

background.note: Red and orange dragons with huge wings who live in the mountains of the Sky Kingdom. They are strong fighters and fast fliers.
A palace of Queen Coral in the Kingdom of the Sea. SkyWings attacked and destroyed it in book 2.

paragraphs.context: Moon’s head snapped up, and she winced as another bolt
paragraphs.simple: Under the noise, Moon hears a clear voice in her mind. It is talking to her, not just thinking.

paragraphs.context: Instinctive fear whipped through Moon’s veins, paralyzing her. All of
paragraphs.simple: Moon is frozen with fear. She remembers all her mother's warnings about strangers.

paragraphs.context: Another telepath — how was that possible? Moon tried to
paragraphs.simple: Moon tries to reach into the speaker's mind, but she cannot. The voice laughs that she has had no training.

paragraphs.context: Did I imagine it? Maybe I imagined it. Maybe the
paragraphs.simple: Moon wonders if she imagined the voice. If it is real, this dragon might teach her, or might tell everyone her secret.

paragraphs.context: Clay! clamored several voices at once in Moon’s head. It’s
paragraphs.simple: Clay arrives, and Moon hears the students' excited thoughts. They think he is a hero.

background.note: Clay is a MudWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is big, kind and loyal.

paragraphs.context: “It’s only the first day, folks,” he said genially. “Nothing
paragraphs.simple: Clay calmly separates the two dragons. He tells Carnelian to calm down and takes Pike away.

background.note: Carnelian is a SkyWing student at Jade Mountain Academy. She is often angry.
Pike is a SeaWing student at Jade Mountain Academy.

paragraphs.context: The SkyWing watched them go with narrow eyes, growling to
paragraphs.simple: The SkyWing comes into Moon's cave without a word, lies on the stone bed and covers her eyes with her wings, still angry.

paragraphs.context: “Oh my gosh, sorry!” it yelped. “I didn’t even see
paragraphs.simple: A small RainWing rushes in. She is smiling, but in her mind she is shocked to share a cave with a NightWing. Her scales stay bright yellow and pink.

paragraphs.context: “Isn’t this exciting? I’m so excited I can hardly STAND
paragraphs.simple: She says she is so excited that she cannot change her scales to a calmer color.

paragraphs.context: “I’m Kinkajou,” the RainWing added, beaming.
paragraphs.simple: The RainWing is called Kinkajou.

background.note: Kinkajou is a young RainWing. She is cheerful, brave and talks a lot.

paragraphs.context: “I love this place,” Kinkajou said. She let go of
paragraphs.simple: Kinkajou is thrilled about the library and the art cave. She cannot read yet, but she is trying hard.

paragraphs.context: “Oh!” Kinkajou said, and her brain went Aha! “I’ve heard
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings once kept Kinkajou as a prisoner, so she is afraid of them. She is glad Moon grew up far from them and says Moon is "hardly a NightWing at all."

paragraphs.context: Moon winced. “Hardly a NightWing at all” was essentially what
paragraphs.simple: The NightWings have thought the same thing about Moon for months. It hurts to hear someone say it out loud.

paragraphs.context: I’m a warrior, the scarlet dragon thought bitterly, keeping her
paragraphs.simple: The SkyWing thinks she is a soldier in Queen Ruby's army and that school is a punishment. She calls her clawmates silly names in her mind.

background.note: Ruby is Queen Scarlet's daughter. After Scarlet loses her throne, Ruby becomes queen of the SkyWings.

paragraphs.context: Kinkajou turned back to Moon, her eyes sparkling. “Ooo, it’s
paragraphs.simple: Kinkajou jokes about guessing the SkyWing's name. Moon tries not to smile because the SkyWing is getting angry.

paragraphs.context: “I have fought in fourteen battles!” the SkyWing thundered. “No
paragraphs.simple: The SkyWing shouts that she has fought in fourteen battles and that no one laughs at her. Then she storms out.

paragraphs.context: There was a pause while Kinkajou got her giggles under
paragraphs.simple: Kinkajou says that being a prisoner of the NightWings and getting hurt in a royal fight should count as battle experience too.

paragraphs.context: “That’s what you slept on while you were growing up
paragraphs.simple: Kinkajou guesses that Moon slept on moss while growing up in the rainforest. She wants to show Moon the library.

paragraphs.context: Moon straightened her shoulders and folded her wings back. It
paragraphs.simple: Moon is scared, but she does not want her first possible friend to think she is boring.

paragraphs.context: Oh, Moonwatcher, my new favorite dragon. This dragonet with her
paragraphs.simple: The voice in her mind says it wants to be Moon's friend.

paragraphs.context: Was there a dragon somewhere reaching out to her? If
paragraphs.simple: Moon wonders who is speaking to her. Could it be another NightWing born with the old powers?

paragraphs.context: Moon couldn’t handle a mystery mind-voice and a new school
paragraphs.simple: Moon pushes her worry about the voice to the back of her mind and tries to keep up with Kinkajou, whose excitement is tiring.

paragraphs.context: “Today is an exploring day,” Kinkajou said with authority. “They
paragraphs.simple: Kinkajou explains that students should explore and find out what interests them.

paragraphs.context: “The dragonets of destiny,” Kinkajou said. “Although they don’t want
paragraphs.simple: The dragonets of destiny started the school. Kinkajou says she is good friends with them, and Sunny and Clay told her the plan because she cannot read the notices yet.

background.note: The five dragonets of the prophecy: Clay, Tsunami, Glory, Starflight and Sunny. 'Destiny' means what is sure to happen in the future.

paragraphs.context: Feel free to explore the whole school today (and every
paragraphs.simple: The notice says students can explore everything, eat in the prey center, join a hunting party with Clay and ask the teachers anything.

paragraphs.context: Kinkajou bounded up a side corridor lined with hanging scrolls
paragraphs.simple: Scrolls with wise sayings hang in the corridor. One says that wisdom is stronger than war.

paragraphs.context: It was like stepping into a dream. Scrolls were everywhere
paragraphs.simple: The library is full of scrolls and cozy places to read. A shy MudWing is reading there.

paragraphs.context: Sunbeams filtered down through skylights in the roof and windows
paragraphs.simple: The windows and skylights are covered with thin green leaves that let light in but keep the wind out.

paragraphs.context: “Hi,” Moon said shyly. There was nothing ever hurtful in
paragraphs.simple: Starflight never thinks unkind things about Moon. Like her, he is an outsider in his own tribe, and he loves scrolls too.

paragraphs.context: “When you want to borrow a scroll,” he said, “you
paragraphs.simple: Starflight explains the library stamps: he stamps a student's name scroll when they borrow a scroll, and stamps it again when they bring it back.

paragraphs.context: “Let me know if I can help you find anything,”
paragraphs.simple: Moon hears Starflight worry about being a blind librarian, but he pushes the worries away. He has memorized the whole library.

paragraphs.context: “It’s all right,” Starflight said. The twinge of sadness in
paragraphs.simple: The MudWing is Sora, one of Clay's sisters.

background.note: Sora is Clay's sister, a MudWing.
